ranking.note: Raised to P1: silent destruction of block data during reindex on supported platforms (*BSD/OmniOS) is data loss, the same consequence class as the other P1 corruption fixes.
Raised to P1: like #36346 it leaves an assumeutxo node aborting in an unrecoverable state that requires a full reindex.
Moved up from 18: an observed std::terminate crash on disk-full is a more certain user-felt stability problem than most other P2s.
Moved up from 21: a node silently stuck unable to advance the chain on block I/O failure outweighs the feature and refactor P2s.
Moved up from 15: masking chainstate read corruption as missing data is a chainstate-integrity hazard, ranked with the other integrity fixes.
Moved up from 23: silent corruption turning unspendable scripts into anyone-can-spend belongs with the integrity cluster, though only reachable via existing corruption.
Moved down from 7: ranked below the live stability/integrity fixes since the cleanup rules are regtest-only, but kept first among the soft-fork implementations.
Downgraded to P2: same consequence class as #32247/#29247 regtest-only opcode implementations with no mainnet activation; it cannot sit a band above its siblings.
Moved down from 11 to sit with the other proposed-opcode implementations, which share its band and consequence.
Raised to P2: prevents reproducible silent chain destruction under -reindex, the same data-loss class as #35524.
Raised to P2: it unblocks batch verification (#29491) and fixes the multithreaded TestBlockValidity script-cache bypass, so it cannot sit below what it unblocks.
Moved down from 12: durable IBD speedup but depends on unmerged upstream secp256k1 work and on #32575, so benefit is the least certain in this band.
Moved down from 17: value is contingent on #35793 landing first; reviewed after its base.
Moved up from 29: ambiguous invalid states feed peer punishment and the kernel API, the strongest correctness claim in this band.
Moved up from 30: removes a real cross-transaction sighash reuse hazard plus an allocation saving in block connection.
Moved up from 33 to sit with the other measured performance work in this band.
Lowered to P3: ~10% block-template validation gain is in the same modest-performance tier as #35195 and #33637.
Moved up from 39: it is the lead PR of the stateless-validation effort and adds substantial isolated consensus test coverage.
Lowered to P3: primarily a kernel C API addition; validation-side consequence is comparable to the other kernel-motivated P3s (#29700, #35557).
Moved down from 34: broad compile-time type-safety refactor with no active bug, ranked below the targeted validation-hygiene items.
Lowered to P4: redundant-traversal and duplicate-log cleanup with no behavioral consequence, same tier as #36066.

inconsistencies: Flush/write-failure cluster: #35714 (P1) is the base for #35731, and #36049, #35003 and #35731 all restructure block/undo write-failure handling. Review #35714 first, then #36049/#35003, then #35731, or the three will conflict.

Error-model cluster: #35646 (remove M_ERROR via util::Expected), #29700 (FlushResult/util::Result returns), #35570 (return BlockValidationState) and #35003 (exceptions vs nullable returns, with an Approach NACK) are competing or dependent takes on the same fatal-error propagation problem. #35646 explicitly unblocks #35570 and should be decided first; a single approach decision would unstick all four.
#32575 is a stated prerequisite for Schnorr batch verification (#29491); review #32575 before #29491.
#35861 (Testnet 5) is built on #35793 (BIP 54) and cannot be evaluated independently; review #35793 first.

Regtest-only soft-fork implementations #31989 (CTV), #32247 (CSFS), #29247 (OP_CAT) and #36122 (CISA) are explicitly designed to compose; they were originally spread across P1-P3 despite identical consequence shape and are now banded together (CISA stays P3 because the author states it is a draft not intended for merge and vendors unmerged secp256k1 work).
Assumeutxo crash pair: #35307 and #36346 fix different triggers of the same outcome (assertion abort during/after snapshot activation requiring reindex) and should be banded and reviewed together.

Reindex data-destruction pair: #35524 (genesis rewrite / AllocateFileRange clobbering) and #35938 (missing xor.dat defaulting to a null key) both prevent silent block-file destruction under -reindex; coordinate so the two startup checks do not overlap.
Modularization chain: #35906, #36066 and #35569 all serve the stateless validation library (#35904); #35906 carries the design and should set the direction for the other two.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: six crash/corruption/data-loss fixes at P1, then a P2 tier mixing stability-and-integrity fixes, measured IBD/block-connection performance, and the regtest-only consensus proposals, then a long P3 tail of validation hygiene, modest performance, and kernel-motivated refactors. Main adjustments were pulling the live corruption/data-loss fixes above the soft-fork implementations, banding the four proposed-opcode PRs together, and lifting #32575 above the batch-verification work it unblocks.
